Sentence (English): We recently purchased this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ QUIET machine ] || ---------------- || We recently purchased this dishwasher. I like that it is very quiet. I mean if you have everything in the house turned off, fans, t.v. etc. you might hear a whisper of a sound. But with things normally running in the house, fans, t.v., a/c, talking, you can not hear this until the very end of the cleaning cycle draining, and even then it's quiet. Cleans well. I really like the third rack at the top. I use it for my larger serving and prepping utensils. Very handy. And the separation in the silverware basket is great. Lots of ways to load the dishwasher. It does not pop open at the end. It does take 2 hours for a cycle. However there is a one hour cycle that I use most. I like the red light dot that shows on the floor letting you know it's running and when it's not lit the cycle is complete. I usually prop it open with a wooden spoon to dry. I wouldn't have to if it popped open at the end. I would recommend this machine because it is priced reasonable for the cycles/options it has, which is enough to get my dishes clean.

My opinion of what could be improved. 1. Status Light - it's great to have a status light that showsn that the machine washing, but I'm disappointed that the white light does not change to a different color to indicate that wash is complete. Instead the light turns off. My former 10 year old Maytag machine had this option but the Bosch 800 does not. 2. The door is a bit flimsy and feels wobly at times. I just doesnt feel very sturdy to me and I wish the door had a more rigid and heavier feel, like most of the current the Kitchen Aid models. 3. Remote Start - I wish that there were a few extra buttons on the machine to schedule the remote start instaed of having to use the app. Overall I'd give this machine a B+.

A felső evőeszközfiók lecsökkenti a másik két fiók hasznos magasságát, viszont maceraberakni az evőeszközöket, és nem is mindíg lesznek tiszták. A korábbi gép esetében a resetelés 3 mp volt. Lett pár funkció, ami eddig a gépről indúlt, de most elő kell hozzá keresni a telefont bejelentkezni, stb. Előnye eddig nem nagyon van a wifi-s dolognak.

Sentence (English): (This review was received as part of a promotion.)
Comments (English): [ Installed after 16.5 years of another 4 series ] || ---------------- || (This review was received as part of a promotion.) We just installed this dishwasher to replace an older Series 4 dishwasher that has served us for 16.5 years. Installing the dishwasher and sliding door was complicated. The template that appears in the installation video and even with the instructions in hand, is not included in the documentation. We had to call assistance and they sent it separately. The instructions to connect it to Home Connect are also not clear or intuitive, the staff who install it do not leave it connected to the home Wi-Fi, they only plug it into the electrical network, water connection and water outlet. They also do not leave the dishwasher flush against the bottom of the counter. In terms of operation, it seems quite quiet and we hope to have it with us for many years. It seems that the cycle times are now much longer if you use ECO programs, the auto program about 2 and a quarter hours, two and a half hours. It has a quick 1 hour program.
Comments (Original): [ Instalado tras 16,5 años de otro serie 4 ] || ---------------- || (Esta reseña se ha recibido a través de una promoción.) Acabamos de instalar este lavavajillas en sustitución de otro anterior de la serie 4 que nos ha dado servicio durante 16,5 años.La instalación del lavavajillas y de la puerta deslizante ha sido complicada. La plantilla que aprece en el video de instalación e incluso ya con las instrucciones en la mano, no esta incluida en la documentación. Hemos tenido que llamar a la asistencia y la envian aparte.Las instrucciones para conectarlo a Home Connect tampoco son claras ni intuitivas, el personal que lo instala, no hacen lo dejan conectado al Wifi de casa, tan sólo enchufan a red electricva, toma de agua y salida de agua. Tampoco dejan nivelado el lavavajillas a ras contra la parte inferior de la encimera.En cuanto a funcionamiento si parece bastante silencioso y esperamos tenerlo con nosotros muchos años. Parece que los tiempos de los ciclos son ahora mucho mas extensos si utilizas programas ECO, el programa auto unas 2 horas y cuarto, dos horas y media. Tiene un programa rápido de 1 hora.

The template that appears in the installation video and even with the instructions in hand, is not included in the documentation. We had to call assistance and they sent it separately. The instructions to connect it to Home Connect are also not clear or intuitive, the staff who install it do not leave it connected to the home Wi-Fi, they only plug it into the electrical network, water connection and water outlet. It seems that the cycle times are now much longer if you use ECO programs, the auto program about 2 and a quarter hours, two and a half hours. It has a quick 1 hour program.

Sentence (English): Had over a dozen various dishwashers in my lifetime.
Comments (English): [ I don't understand why other dishwashers exist ] || ---------------- || Had over a dozen various dishwashers in my lifetime. The last good one was a Bosch SMS88 till we sold that house and moved to a place where the prev. owner put in a fisher paykel double dishdrawer just prior to auction. What a woeful POS that was. After 2months I'd had enough and sold it. Went shopping and used the money to buy an Asko DBI565 in white to match cabinetry. I am blown away by how good it is at doing its one job. washing dishes. It's that good at it, that I don't know why I bought the Bosch way back when. and also just can't fathom why for the same money, you get dishwashers that don't wash dishes, let alone anywhere near as good as this does.In my experience, everything comes out polished. It's quiet. I run the hygiene program mostly, in an hour a full load is spotless. My wife and I would normally rinse everything before putting in the dishwasher of the day but now. we just fork or spoon off the food waste prior and then chuck em straight in with NO rinsing. Incredible.My bbq steel trays come out almost new. Never happened before in any dishwasher.It tells me when I'm low on rinse aid, I mean that's a 1st world thing but why doesn't every dishwasher tell you that? Even more, we've done about 10 or so loads since ownership and have rinse aid on setting 4 out of 5. Means it's using the second highest amount of rinse aid per wash. I thought maybe the sensor isn't working because I'd only filled rinse aid when installed. So I topped it. Barely needed 10ml. And the dishes come out immaculate. Seriously. I'm as baffled as anyone how it's this good. The fisher needed rinse aid every 3rd loads the Bosch every 4th. Here after 10 I can go another 20 loads before refilling rinse aid.Oh and the door pops open when it's finished on some programs which i think is so the dishes dry and cool faster. nice touch.I then decided to rewash everything we had in the kitchen. I fit everything without skipping slots. 2 loads. Probably over 25 place settings in total. Hahaha. I seriously do not understand how or why many other products exist, sell for the same or near enough to the same price and yet do less than half as good a job. Even my SMS88 was one that seriously should be commended for being half as good as this. All other manufacturers should benchmark themselves against this DBI565 model from Asko.I love it. If Asko makes it, i'm convinced I'm never buying any other brand.

It's that good at it, that I don't know why I bought the Bosch way back when. and also just can't fathom why for the same money, you get dishwashers that don't wash dishes, let alone anywhere near as good as this does.In my experience, everything comes out polished. It's quiet. I run the hygiene program mostly, in an hour a full load is spotless. My wife and I would normally rinse everything before putting in the dishwasher of the day but now. we just fork or spoon off the food waste prior and then chuck em straight in with NO rinsing. Incredible.My bbq steel trays come out almost new. Never happened before in any dishwasher.It tells me when I'm low on rinse aid, I mean that's a 1st world thing but why doesn't every dishwasher tell you that? Even more, we've done about 10 or so loads since ownership and have rinse aid on setting 4 out of 5. Means it's using the second highest amount of rinse aid per wash. I thought maybe the sensor isn't working because I'd only filled rinse aid when installed. So I topped it. Barely needed 10ml. And the dishes come out immaculate. Seriously. Sentence (English): I used to use a 12-place setting dishwasher, but after moving, I felt like I couldn't live without one, so I ended up buying one.
Comments (English): I used to use a 12-place setting dishwasher, but after moving, I felt like I couldn't live without one, so I ended up buying one. I agonized over whether to get the 12-place or 6-place setting. I decided to wait until I moved into my actual home to buy the 12-place one, so I purchased the 6-place setting. The reason I bought it was because I heard it's good for "Tetrising" dishes. I chose it because it has a single tier. It looks neat and pretty. Maybe because I'm not good at Tetris, stacking dishes is a bit inconvenient. I bought Magic Hand pots specifically for dishwashing, so putting them in isn't a problem. It's perfect for a household of two. I rinse off food residue with water before putting them in the dishwasher. However, I don't really get the feeling that they are being cleaned thoroughly yet. There are faint traces remaining on coffee cups and the walls of pots from boiling soup. Food residue on the cutlery is still there, too. I don't mind water pooling because I just accept it as normal, but... Water droplets form on the overturned dishes, sometimes remaining there until the next morning or lunchtime. Also, while I was deliberating, I watched a lot of YouTube and blog reviews, but nobody mentioned the noise. I was in the room putting the baby to sleep while the dishwasher was running, and I was terrified; I shuddered. The sound of the water turning on and the drainage was so loud that I thought the product was defective. I am still trying to get used to it. Fortunately, as time passes and I use it more often, the sound is getting quieter. Still, I can't help but flinch. I developed eczema on my hands, so they were cracked, bleeding, and itchy. Since I bought this to improve my quality of life, I am somewhat satisfied. I think it is inevitable that I feel it is lacking a bit because I used to use a 12-place setting model. You can't avoid getting soap on your hands at all when using a dishwasher. It is 9 times better than having nothing; 10 times better... ;;. Still, if you can afford it, I would recommend buying it. A review written much later. I am using it very well, and I have gotten used to the noise, so I just accept it as it is. I agonized over whether to get the 12-place or 6-place setting. I decided to wait until I moved into my actual home to buy the 12-place one, so I purchased the 6-place setting. The reason I bought it was because I heard it's good for "Tetrising" dishes. I chose it because it has a single tier. It looks neat and pretty. Maybe because I'm not good at Tetris, stacking dishes is a bit inconvenient. I bought Magic Hand pots specifically for dishwashing, so putting them in isn't a problem. It's perfect for a household of two. I rinse off food residue with water before putting them in the dishwasher. However, I don't really get the feeling that they are being cleaned thoroughly yet. There are faint traces remaining on coffee cups and the walls of pots from boiling soup. Food residue on the cutlery is still there, too. I don't mind water pooling because I just accept it as normal, but... Water droplets form on the overturned dishes, sometimes remaining there until the next morning or lunchtime. Also, while I was deliberating, I watched a lot of YouTube and blog reviews, but nobody mentioned the noise. I was in the room putting the baby to sleep while the dishwasher was running, and I was terrified; I shuddered. The sound of the water turning on and the drainage was so loud that I thought the product was defective. I am still trying to get used to it. Fortunately, as time passes and I use it more often, the sound is getting quieter. Still, I can't help but flinch. I developed eczema on my hands, so they were cracked, bleeding, and itchy. Since I bought this to improve my quality of life, I am somewhat satisfied. I think it is inevitable that I feel it is lacking a bit because I used to use a 12-place setting model. You can't avoid getting soap on your hands at all when using a dishwasher. It is 9 times better than having nothing; 10 times better... ;;. Still, if you can afford it, I would recommend buying it. A review written much later. I am using it very well, and I have gotten used to the noise, so I just accept it as it is. As for moisture and stains, the concerns I mentioned earlier disappeared after I switched detergents. It is now an appliance I can't live without. However, as my family has grown and my laziness has kicked in, I still feel that the 6-place setting is too small. Nevertheless, I love it. It hasn't broken down yet, either. I am using it well!

I agonized over whether to get the 12-place or 6-place setting. I decided to wait until I moved into my actual home to buy the 12-place one, so I purchased the 6-place setting. The reason I bought it was because I heard it's good for "Tetrising" dishes. I chose it because it has a single tier. It looks neat and pretty. Maybe because I'm not good at Tetris, stacking dishes is a bit inconvenient. I bought Magic Hand pots specifically for dishwashing, so putting them in isn't a problem. It's perfect for a household of two. I rinse off food residue with water before putting them in the dishwasher. However, I don't really get the feeling that they are being cleaned thoroughly yet. There are faint traces remaining on coffee cups and the walls of pots from boiling soup. Food residue on the cutlery is still there, too. I don't mind water pooling because I just accept it as normal, but... Water droplets form on the overturned dishes, sometimes remaining there until the next morning or lunchtime. Also, while I was deliberating, I watched a lot of YouTube and blog reviews, but nobody mentioned the noise. I was in the room putting the baby to sleep while the dishwasher was running, and I was terrified; I shuddered. The sound of the water turning on and the drainage was so loud that I thought the product was defective. I am still trying to get used to it. Fortunately, as time passes and I use it more often, the sound is getting quieter. Still, I can't help but flinch. I developed eczema on my hands, so they were cracked, bleeding, and itchy. Since I bought this to improve my quality of life, I am somewhat satisfied. I think it is inevitable that I feel it is lacking a bit because I used to use a 12-place setting model. You can't avoid getting soap on your hands at all when using a dishwasher. It is 9 times better than having nothing; 10 times better... ;;. Still, if you can afford it, I would recommend buying it. A review written much later. I am using it very well, and I have gotten used to the noise, so I just accept it as it is. As for moisture and stains, the concerns I mentioned earlier disappeared after I switched detergents. It is now an appliance I can't live without. However, as my family has grown and my laziness has kicked in, I still feel that the 6-place setting is too small. Nevertheless, I love it. It hasn't broken down yet, either. I am using it well!

I agonized over whether to get the 12-place or 6-place setting. I decided to wait until I moved into my actual home to buy the 12-place one, so I purchased the 6-place setting. The reason I bought it was because I heard it's good for "Tetrising" dishes. I chose it because it has a single tier. It looks neat and pretty. Maybe because I'm not good at Tetris, stacking dishes is a bit inconvenient. I bought Magic Hand pots specifically for dishwashing, so putting them in isn't a problem. It's perfect for a household of two. I rinse off food residue with water before putting them in the dishwasher. However, I don't really get the feeling that they are being cleaned thoroughly yet. There are faint traces remaining on coffee cups and the walls of pots from boiling soup. Food residue on the cutlery is still there, too. I don't mind water pooling because I just accept it as normal, but... Water droplets form on the overturned dishes, sometimes remaining there until the next morning or lunchtime. Also, while I was deliberating, I watched a lot of YouTube and blog reviews, but nobody mentioned the noise. I was in the room putting the baby to sleep while the dishwasher was running, and I was terrified; I shuddered. The sound of the water turning on and the drainage was so loud that I thought the product was defective. I am still trying to get used to it. Fortunately, as time passes and I use it more often, the sound is getting quieter. Still, I can't help but flinch. I developed eczema on my hands, so they were cracked, bleeding, and itchy. Since I bought this to improve my quality of life, I am somewhat satisfied. I think it is inevitable that I feel it is lacking a bit because I used to use a 12-place setting model. You can't avoid getting soap on your hands at all when using a dishwasher. It is 9 times better than having nothing; 10 times better... ;;. Still, if you can afford it, I would recommend buying it. A review written much later. I am using it very well, and I have gotten used to the noise, so I just accept it as it is. As for moisture and stains, the concerns I mentioned earlier disappeared after I switched detergents. It is now an appliance I can't live without. However, as my family has grown and my laziness has kicked in, I still feel that the 6-place setting is too small. Nevertheless, I love it. It hasn't broken down yet, either. I am using it well!

I agonized over whether to get the 12-place or 6-place setting. I decided to wait until I moved into my actual home to buy the 12-place one, so I purchased the 6-place setting. The reason I bought it was because I heard it's good for "Tetrising" dishes. I chose it because it has a single tier. It looks neat and pretty. Maybe because I'm not good at Tetris, stacking dishes is a bit inconvenient. I bought Magic Hand pots specifically for dishwashing, so putting them in isn't a problem. It's perfect for a household of two. I rinse off food residue with water before putting them in the dishwasher. However, I don't really get the feeling that they are being cleaned thoroughly yet. There are faint traces remaining on coffee cups and the walls of pots from boiling soup. Food residue on the cutlery is still there, too. I don't mind water pooling because I just accept it as normal, but... Water droplets form on the overturned dishes, sometimes remaining there until the next morning or lunchtime. Also, while I was deliberating, I watched a lot of YouTube and blog reviews, but nobody mentioned the noise. I was in the room putting the baby to sleep while the dishwasher was running, and I was terrified; I shuddered. The sound of the water turning on and the drainage was so loud that I thought the product was defective. I am still trying to get used to it. Fortunately, as time passes and I use it more often, the sound is getting quieter. Still, I can't help but flinch. I developed eczema on my hands, so they were cracked, bleeding, and itchy. Since I bought this to improve my quality of life, I am somewhat satisfied. I think it is inevitable that I feel it is lacking a bit because I used to use a 12-place setting model. You can't avoid getting soap on your hands at all when using a dishwasher. It is 9 times better than having nothing; 10 times better... ;;. Still, if you can afford it, I would recommend buying it. A review written much later. I am using it very well, and I have gotten used to the noise, so I just accept it as it is. As for moisture and stains, the concerns I mentioned earlier disappeared after I switched detergents. It is now an appliance I can't live without. However, as my family has grown and my laziness has kicked in, I still feel that the 6-place setting is too small. Nevertheless, I love it. It hasn't broken down yet, either. I am using it well!

I agonized over whether to get the 12-place or 6-place setting. I decided to wait until I moved into my actual home to buy the 12-place one, so I purchased the 6-place setting. The reason I bought it was because I heard it's good for "Tetrising" dishes. I chose it because it has a single tier. It looks neat and pretty. Maybe because I'm not good at Tetris, stacking dishes is a bit inconvenient. I bought Magic Hand pots specifically for dishwashing, so putting them in isn't a problem. It's perfect for a household of two. I rinse off food residue with water before putting them in the dishwasher. However, I don't really get the feeling that they are being cleaned thoroughly yet. There are faint traces remaining on coffee cups and the walls of pots from boiling soup. Food residue on the cutlery is still there, too. I don't mind water pooling because I just accept it as normal, but... Water droplets form on the overturned dishes, sometimes remaining there until the next morning or lunchtime. Also, while I was deliberating, I watched a lot of YouTube and blog reviews, but nobody mentioned the noise. I was in the room putting the baby to sleep while the dishwasher was running, and I was terrified; I shuddered. The sound of the water turning on and the drainage was so loud that I thought the product was defective. I am still trying to get used to it. Fortunately, as time passes and I use it more often, the sound is getting quieter. Still, I can't help but flinch. I developed eczema on my hands, so they were cracked, bleeding, and itchy. Since I bought this to improve my quality of life, I am somewhat satisfied. I think it is inevitable that I feel it is lacking a bit because I used to use a 12-place setting model. You can't avoid getting soap on your hands at all when using a dishwasher. It is 9 times better than having nothing; 10 times better... ;;. Still, if you can afford it, I would recommend buying it. A review written much later. I am using it very well, and I have gotten used to the noise, so I just accept it as it is. As for moisture and stains, the concerns I mentioned earlier disappeared after I switched detergents. It is now an appliance I can't live without. However, as my family has grown and my laziness has kicked in, I still feel that the 6-place setting is too small. Nevertheless, I love it. It hasn't broken down yet, either. I am using it well!

Sentence (English): We love our Bosch 300 Series Dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Incredibly Quiet, Cleans Well - One Minor Flaw ] || ---------------- || We love our Bosch 300 Series Dishwasher. Our older dishwasher wasn't broken but was in dire need of an upgrade. It was often too loud to have conversations in the kitchen. It also did a poor job of cleaning. This dishwasher is in a completely different world from that old dishwasher. The three racks for everything means we don't have to fight to get all of our dishes in while fighting for space from utensils. We're a family of 7 - so there's lots of dishes! My only gripe with this dishwasher is that once the bottom rack is fully pulled out in order to load or unload, it is very easy to slip off the guides and it needs adjustment to get it back on track. I understand that it's nitpicky - but it's really the only negative. We've used every setting on this dishwasher and when our refrigerator failed earlier this year, this experience was the reason we bought a Bosch refrigerator. 10/10 would buy again.

Sentence (English): Time of ownership: 11 months.
Comments (English): [ Works great ] || ---------------- || Time of ownership: 11 months. I am very satisfied with this dishwasher. If you use good detergent like the Cascade Platinum pods, you don't need to pre-rinse your dishes. I use the automatic wash (ProWash) and the heated wash as my only cycle options every time. The water sure feels hot whenever I open the dishwasher mid-cycle. Even without the quieting foam, it operates very quietly. I cannot tell if it's in a wash or dry cycle from its sound. Four stars and not five, because plastic dishes won't be dry under the standard drying cycle unless they sit in the closed, hot tub for over four hours. And things don't always get clean when they are placed on the utensil part of the third rack -- there is no dedicated sprayer there, so things don't get quite as clean there unless they aren't visibly dirty when you put something there. I bought this for $1,050 during a time of frequent appliance shortages. Now with the price down to $900, this is quite a competitively priced dishwasher. Since it's made by Whirlpool, you can expect parts to be easily available years from now -- both OEM and aftermarket -- unlike some other manufacturers. At nearly a year of ownership I cannot judge its longevity, but it's nice knowing that I won't throw out an appliance due to the lack of parts available for it. This can be a frequent problem with some manufacturers like Samsung or Frigidaire. I heard from a repair company that getting parts for Bosch dishwashers was a problem during the pandemic, but was not a problem for Whirlpool parts.

Sentence (English): The Samsung Bespoke dishwasher is the perfect addition to my kitchen appliances.
Comments (English): [ Best investment! ] || ---------------- || The Samsung Bespoke dishwasher is the perfect addition to my kitchen appliances. Not only is it the perfect fit under my island countertop but it blends in so well with the White Glass finish. As with any Bespoke series appliances by Samsung, one can easily swap the front finishes to different colors but the white glass finish ended up being our choice to blend well with our bespoke refrigerator and the gray/shiny cabinets we have. It was professionally installed for us so I cannot speak to ease of installation but I can say that something important to note is that if installing yourself, make sure that the final installation is perfectly plumb with the countertop as we found out during install that our countertop wasn't leveled perfectly so we had to adjust the dishwasher slightly. Not a show stopper.Now for the fun part, the features. This dishwasher is as quiet as it gets, I have no issues watching a movie in the living room and have the dishwasher running at the same time with no interruptions or any sound issues. It comes in at a whopping 46dba which is very low noise level. I absolutely love how loaded it is with different cycles and features. For starters, you can easily add it to the smart things app by Samsung. I have a Samsung galaxy phone so integration with smart things was even more seamless. It automatically detected the dishwasher the moment I turned on smart things and added it successfully. Make sure you link it to your home wifi as well as it does have a built-in smart control function which allows you to remotely control the dishwasher through the app/phone. I am able to see when it finishes, when it's running, and select different cycles all remotely. I am also able to start the dishwasher and stop it if I so desire. There are different cycles available but I absolutely love the set and forget it cycle which is called AUTO. I let it automatically detect soil level and cycle accordingly with the right amount of energy and water as needed. To me this is roughly a 2.5 hrs cycle which works well and I get clean dishes every time. The remaining cycles are 'normal', 'heavy', 'delicate', express 60, preblast, download cycle. Most of these are self-explanatory except the preblast and download cycle. The preblast cycle helps with making sure if your pots for example are heavily soiled, it will turn on the turboblaster (yellow jet disk bottom left corner) feature which is pressurized jets that will help clear out the majority of stuck on soiled food. The express 60 is also great because it finishes the whole cycle in 1 hour in case there is an urgency to get dishes clean faster or multiple rounds are needed after a party etc. It takes standard HE detergent powder, liquid, or tabs. I personally like the tabs as it's an all in one and the outcome is super clean dishes. The rinse aid compartment is also available if you choose to use it. The download cycle is unique in that you can select on the app special cycles such as baby items, night mode, plastics, or pots and pans. Each with different properties depending on what you are washing. It also has a delay start up to 24hrs which is great if you do not want your hot water to run out while you are showering so I set mine at 2am delay start when everyone is asleep with no issues as it will be ready by morning. Another unique feature of this dishwasher is the drying method. Not only does it have the traditional electric drying but it also auto opens the door at the end of cycle to get fresh air in to aid in the drying process. I must say I haven't had any issues with wet dishes when I take the dishes out compared to my old dishwasher. I also didn't experience any etching or any film on any of my glasses or dishes. Of course, I will point out that I do have a water softener installed so it definitely helps with making sure I don't have hard water while the dishwasher is running.This dishwasher comes with 3 racks with top rack to be used for flatware or any cooking utensils, middle rack (typically top) on traditional dishwashers to be used for cups and bowls, and bottom rack for pots/pans/dishes. I love that the bottom and middle racks are adjustable in height and also that the 3rd top rack can be completely removed if necessary or if not utilized to give extra clearance for larger glasses or cups/bowls. Overall this dishwasher I can simply say is unique in features, design, ease of use, and does the most important job that matters well – clean the dishes. I am confident that my dishes are clean and sanitized and I am saving energy and water doing so compared to hand washing. I would highly recommend this dishwasher to anyone looking for a do it all dishwasher that is quiet and performs really well.

Sentence (English): My previous dishwasher was a Kenmore Elite 11 years old.
Comments (English): [ Worth the price of admission ] || ---------------- || My previous dishwasher was a Kenmore Elite 11 years old. it was a top tier model and much quieter than earlier dishwashers I had. It cleaned OK. I have hard well water and keeping the interior clean was a struggle, and dishes and glasses always developed cloudy films, regardless of soap brand or rinse aids. Dishes took a long time to dry. The water filter clogged often and dishes needed to be pretty clean before loading to get reasonable results. So I needed a better dishwasher. After looking at many different brands and models, I decided this Bosch model seemed to have the important things I wanted. It took a lot of explaining to my wife as to why the cost of this was neqar;y twice what a similar to our old appliance would cost. After the first load of dishes, my wife understood why this unit was worth it. By the second load, I was able to get the Salt needed for water softening. The second load was even better than the first. The water softener allowed the detergent to work better, the dishes were cleaner, old stains fon dishes and cutting boards have been removed, the glasses, even the filmed over ones, came out clean and shiny, no film. We are cycling our dishes through the washer as they come out clean, film free, sanitized and dry. As quiet as our previous dishwasher was, this one is nearly undetectable. I have an air gap type drain, so the only noise heard is when the water drains. Also, the filter does not clog up, and is easay to clean, unlike my old dishwasher. So, what makes this worth the money? 1. Softenens hard water for better cleaning and no cloudy films 2. Gets the dishes extemely clean and sanitized. Glasses clean and shiny with no film (no film on dishes either). 3. You can barely tell it's running. 4. Has a very large interior. 5. Interior racks have many adjustments. 6. Interior lighting 7. Network app allows for great customization of the wash cycle. 8. Dishes are DRY when the dishwasher finishes. 9. Looks great, works great. I don't know if there are better machines than this, as I have not tried other brands, but this dishwasher does everything in an excellent manner. It delivers on the promise of quiet, clean dishes, great flexibilty. It is worth the price.

Sentence (English): My previous dishwasher was a Kenmore Elite 11 years old.
Comments (English): [ Worth the price of admission ] || ---------------- || My previous dishwasher was a Kenmore Elite 11 years old. it was a top tier model and much quieter than earlier dishwashers I had. It cleaned OK. I have hard well water and keeping the interior clean was a struggle, and dishes and glasses always developed cloudy films, regardless of soap brand or rinse aids. Dishes took a long time to dry. The water filter clogged often and dishes needed to be pretty clean before loading to get reasonable results. So I needed a better dishwasher. After looking at many different brands and models, I decided this Bosch model seemed to have the important things I wanted. It took a lot of explaining to my wife as to why the cost of this was neqar;y twice what a similar to our old appliance would cost. After the first load of dishes, my wife understood why this unit was worth it. By the second load, I was able to get the Salt needed for water softening. The second load was even better than the first. The water softener allowed the detergent to work better, the dishes were cleaner, old stains fon dishes and cutting boards have been removed, the glasses, even the filmed over ones, came out clean and shiny, no film. We are cycling our dishes through the washer as they come out clean, film free, sanitized and dry. As quiet as our previous dishwasher was, this one is nearly undetectable. I have an air gap type drain, so the only noise heard is when the water drains. Also, the filter does not clog up, and is easay to clean, unlike my old dishwasher. So, what makes this worth the money? 1. Softenens hard water for better cleaning and no cloudy films 2. Gets the dishes extemely clean and sanitized. Glasses clean and shiny with no film (no film on dishes either). 3. You can barely tell it's running. 4. Has a very large interior. 5. Interior racks have many adjustments.6. Interior lighting7. Network app allows for great customization of the wash cycle. 8. Dishes are DRY when the dishwasher finishes. 9. Looks great, works great. I don't know if there are better machines than this, as I have not tried other brands, but this dishwasher does everything in an excellent manner. It delivers on the promise of quiet, clean dishes, great flexibilty. It is worth the price.

Sentence (English): We had a Bosch 800 series that lasted about ten years.
Comments (English): [ Replacement Bosch 800 ] || ---------------- || We had a Bosch 800 series that lasted about ten years. The expected repair cost (~$400 when it developed a leak of indeterminate origin) was too high for an appliance of that age, so we opted to buy new. Unfortunately, the new 800 series made in teh US wasn't available, but this German-made model was. It cleans well -- just like the old one. The Crystal Dry feature works great. Plastic items like food storage containers do come out dry, for the most part. In this respect, the new model is better than the old. Also, everyone in the family agrees that the control panel is incrementally better than the old one. Oddly, where this model seems to have taken a step back is in the layout of the three trays. The top tray is a little more adjustable, though that hasn't really benefited us. It just seems a little more complicated/busy. The spacing of the tines on the second tray is different but fine; call it a neutral change. The bottom tray still has us puzzling, even after a month's use. The layout simply seems a lot less convenient, unless all you use are dinner plates. We find it difficult to conveniently fit larger items like mixing bowls, baking dishes, etc. This design change definitely let us down. Still and all, it's a nice washer. It's quiet and it cleans well. I suppose we'll eventually figure out how to get the most out of the bottom tray.

Just gotta fry them before putting them away.

Sentence (English): We chose this dishwasher based on a few factors - one of which is the versatility of the various drawers.
Comments (English): [ Still great after 2 years ] || ---------------- || We chose this dishwasher based on a few factors - one of which is the versatility of the various drawers. Another being the dedicated cutlery drawer. One of the great features are the fold-out racks in each drawer. This allows you to adjust for either lots of plates, or big pans, or a combination. Particularly useful are that some of the racks have 3 alternate sets of tines - meaning you can have either narrow or wide spaced racks to suit different sized plates. The middle drawer is height adjustable (and easy to use) plus the cutlery drawer has a drop-down section to create space for larger items. For us, these features are well thought out and make this a stand-out compared to others. The washing modes are good - plenty of options. The runs-times are perhaps a bit long (from just under 1hr to over 2.5hrs) 2 years down the track an it still works great. No issues (hope this review doesn't jinx it though! ). Would definitely recommend.

Comments (English): [ Nice portable dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Does a good job cleaning and I love the butcher block top. Minor annoyance is that the buttons don't light up until pressed. Scared me when I first plugged it in and saw no signs of life. The buttons do light once pressed and the clean light comes on when it's done. The Normal cycle takes approx. 2 hours, but it has a 1-hour cycle mode that I have not tried. The top rack is roomy, small plates fit in it, and the bottom rack (large plates and pots and pans) has so far accomodated everything I've tried to wash in it. This dishwasher is a workhorse, and I hope it remains so for years to come.

Sentence (English): I was very hesitant as it was my first time buying a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ I was very hesitant as it was my first time buying a dishwasher. Trial and error during installation. ] || ---------------- || I was very hesitant as it was my first time buying a dishwasher. There was some trial and error during installation ^^ Because I didn't know much, I didn't tell the interior design manager who was moving that the sink had to be installed perfectly. Since the owner of the interior construction company is not a professional installer of dishwashers, he also postponed all finishing work because he thought he might need to change the sink to fit the dishwasher. So, it was a very tedious installation that put both the dishwasher installer and interior design manager in a difficult position. . I went back and forth on whether to use a water filter or not and couldn't decide, but I think I did the right thing ^^. It was an old single-family house, so waterworks were done, but the boiler pipes were not replaced, so the hot water was coming out red. I almost drank red water. I almost couldn't use the dishwasher for a while;; It was eventful in one way or another. I think I made a good purchase. I had a hard time since I moved, but washing dishes has become easier.

Sentence (English): More than happy.
Comments (English): [ Fantastic dishwasher ] || ---------------- || More than happy. I originally purchased a different brand that was 2-3x the price and looked really nice, and was "feature-packed" I thought. It didn't end up fitting because of a measuring error. So glad it didn't. I went with this instead. It has everything I wanted and more. EXCEPT for a stainless steel interior. I was hung up on that for a bit. but I don't think I needed it and am very happy with this dishwasher. It does a great job, and is feature loaded. There are few dishwashers at this price that have and actual heating element to dry. this does! It quiet enough, quick enough, and has a 3rd rack, bottle jets, sanitize/steam option, extra hot water, 2 drying settings if you choose to use it, and more. I highly recommend it for the cost, features, functionality. I would choose this over the other 2-3x unit I looked at even if I had space for the other.

Sentence (English): In fact, one of the misconceptions about dishwashers is that they use a lot of water, electricity, and detergent, and that they do not need to pre-wash the dishes.
Comments (English): In fact, one of the misconceptions about dishwashers is that they use a lot of water, electricity, and detergent, and that they do not need to pre-wash the dishes. I am one of those who thought, "Why bother? If you just wash them and throw them away, you can just be a little more diligent. Why bother?" But then I hit menopause at 50 and my finger joints started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't invest this much in myself~~" When I was selected for the experience group, I was thrilled. I found out that there are also compact sizes that can fit 3-4 people in a small space. The models that are coming out these days have good performance and they say that they clean well even without pre-washing. I guess it's an improvement. But personally, I think pre-washing the dishes is a way to solve the hassle of not having to do the secondary manual work to remove grease or seasoning. The monthly electricity bill for 6 people is 2,000-3,000 won. It can be done for less than 100 won for 4 people, so let's put aside the burden for a moment~ Opening soon~~~~~ Roughly 40cm in width, length, and height. It's a cube shape with a soft curve. Among the components, our spoon is made of wood, so we plan to use it without inserting the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose was not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is an easy way to tighten it by inserting it into the drain hole. When supplying water manually, you must press the power button 'be sure' to supply water to check the water tank alarm sound. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) is said to be suitable for basic washing because the amount of water is small, but it takes 1 hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) 29 minutes. The only regret is that there is no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. You also have to use a 'detergent for washing'. Since it was my first time, I searched and bought a detergent that worked well among the ones I tested. I just put it on a square tray without a spout and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablet, it'll fall to the floor when I close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to be? (It just falls.) When washing larger dishes, you can fold the secret bar to make better use of space, and it has wheels so you don't have to put your hands deep inside, which is convenient. It doesn't make much noise, and I think the force of the spray from below is strong. Hot water comes out when you drain it. It's not enough to burn you, but you have to be careful. I feel like my quality of life has improved since I was freed from the housework of washing dishes. I like how it makes me smile when I see clean dishes. If you feel this way, I'd like to recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be good to use it for 2~3 people in the future. It's a little short on space, and it would be better if a drying function was added separately, not for washing. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.
Comments (Original): 사실상 식기세척기 오해중에 하나가 물,전기,세제 양이 많고 애벌설겆이를 하는데 굳이.. 참말로 그냥 씻어 엎으면되는걸 게을러서 조금만 부지런을 떨면될것을 굳이..왜..라고 생각했던 사람중 한사람이 접니다. 그런데 50에 갱년기가 겹치고 손가락 관절 마디마디가 쑤시기 시작했고 갑자기 인생사 뭐있나..나한테 이정도도 투자못하겠어~~지름신 함 불러내지 할때 체험단에 선정되어 신이 났습니다. 작은공간에 3~4인기준 넘 아담한 사이즈도 있다는걸 알았네요. 요즘 나오는 모델들은 성능도 좋고 애벌설겆이를 안해도 깨끗한 세척이된다고 합니다. 개선이 된거겠죠. 그래도 개인적인 생각으론 기름때나 벌건 양념은 애벌을 해주는게 2차 수작업으로 가지않는 번거로움 해결방법이지 않을까 싶어요. 6인 기준으로 한달 전기요금이 2~3천원 나온대요. 4인기준 한번 돌리는데 백원 미만으로도 나올수 있다니 부담감은 잠시 접어두고~ 개봉박두~~~~~ 대충 가로 세로 높이가 40cm. 부드러운 곡선의 큐브모양이예요. 구성품중에 저흰 수저가 목재여서 수저통은 끼우지않고 사용하려합니다. 모든  식기가 세척에 적합하질않아 확인도 필수. 입수호스는 연결하지않았고 배수호수는(길이145cm정도)배수구멍에 콕끼워 조임새로 쪼는 쉬운 방식입니다. 수동급수시에는 '꼭' 전원버튼을 누른 후 급수를해야 물탱크 알림음 확인할수 있습니다. 작동버튼중에 표준코스(세척65도-헹굼-헹굼70도-건조)가 물의 양이 적고 기본 세척에 적합하다는데 시간이 1시간이나 걸려서 시간이 짧은 쾌속 (세척55도-헹굼-헹굼60도)29분으로 사용해볼까 생각중입니다. 아쉬운건 건조 기능이없어 문을 열어 말려야합니다. 또 '세척전용세제'를 써야된데요. 첨인지라 검색을 해보니 세정제 실험한것중에 성능 좋은걸루 구매했어요.  주입구가 없는 그냥 사각 트레이 모양에  얹고 문을 닫아요. 근데 액상이든 타블렛이든 문을 닫으면 바닥으로 떨어지겠는데 원래가 이런 방식인건가? (그냥 떨어지네요 ㅋㅋ) 좀 큰그릇 세척시엔 시크릿바를 접을수 있어 공간활용도 되고 이동바퀴가 있어 깊숙이 손을 넣을 필요도 없이 편합니다. 생활소음정도  크진않고 밑에서 쏘는 힘이 쎈가봐요. 배수때 뜨거운물이 빠져요. 화상입을정도는 아니여도 조심해야겠습니다. 설겆이라는 가사노동에서 해방되면서 맘적으로 삶의 질이 높아진 느낌이랄까... 뽀득뽀득한 그릇을 보니 웃음이 나는게 기부니가 좋아졌어요. 이런 맘이면 식기세척기 추천해드리고 싶네요..  추후-2~3인용으로 사용하면 좋을듯 싶어요. 공간이 살짝 부족하고 세척용도가 아닌 건조기능이 따로 추가가되면 더 좋겠어요 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료로 제공 받아 작성한 구매 후기입니다.

Sentence (English): Why bother?"
Comments (English): In fact, one of the misconceptions about dishwashers is that they use a lot of water, electricity, and detergent, and that they do not need to pre-wash the dishes. I am one of those who thought, "Why bother? If you just wash them and throw them away, you can just be a little more diligent. Why bother?" But then I hit menopause at 50 and my finger joints started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't invest this much in myself~~" When I was selected for the experience group, I was thrilled. I found out that there are also compact sizes that can fit 3-4 people in a small space. The models that are coming out these days have good performance and they say that they clean well even without pre-washing. I guess it's an improvement. But personally, I think pre-washing the dishes is a way to solve the hassle of not having to do the secondary manual work to remove grease or seasoning. The monthly electricity bill for 6 people is 2,000-3,000 won. It can be done for less than 100 won for 4 people, so let's put aside the burden for a moment~ Opening soon~~~~~ Roughly 40cm in width, length, and height. It's a cube shape with a soft curve. Among the components, our spoon is made of wood, so we plan to use it without inserting the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose was not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is an easy way to tighten it by inserting it into the drain hole. When supplying water manually, you must press the power button 'be sure' to supply water to check the water tank alarm sound. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) is said to be suitable for basic washing because the amount of water is small, but it takes 1 hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) 29 minutes. The only regret is that there is no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. You also have to use a 'detergent for washing'. Since it was my first time, I searched and bought a detergent that worked well among the ones I tested. I just put it on a square tray without a spout and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablet, it'll fall to the floor when I close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to be? (It just falls.) When washing larger dishes, you can fold the secret bar to make better use of space, and it has wheels so you don't have to put your hands deep inside, which is convenient. It doesn't make much noise, and I think the force of the spray from below is strong. Hot water comes out when you drain it. It's not enough to burn you, but you have to be careful. I feel like my quality of life has improved since I was freed from the housework of washing dishes. I like how it makes me smile when I see clean dishes. If you feel this way, I'd like to recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be good to use it for 2~3 people in the future. It's a little short on space, and it would be better if a drying function was added separately, not for washing. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

It's a little short on space, and it would be better if a drying function was added separately, not for washing. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

(그냥 떨어지네요 ㅋㅋ) 좀 큰그릇 세척시엔 시크릿바를 접을수 있어 공간활용도 되고 이동바퀴가 있어 깊숙이 손을 넣을 필요도 없이 편합니다. 생활소음정도  크진않고 밑에서 쏘는 힘이 쎈가봐요. 배수때 뜨거운물이 빠져요. 화상입을정도는 아니여도 조심해야겠습니다. 설겆이라는 가사노동에서 해방되면서 맘적으로 삶의 질이 높아진 느낌이랄까... 뽀득뽀득한 그릇을 보니 웃음이 나는게 기부니가 좋아졌어요. 이런 맘이면 식기세척기 추천해드리고 싶네요..  추후-2~3인용으로 사용하면 좋을듯 싶어요. 공간이 살짝 부족하고 세척용도가 아닌 건조기능이 따로 추가가되면 더 좋겠어요 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료로 제공 받아 작성한 구매 후기입니다.

Sentence (English): I guess it's an improvement.
Comments (English): In fact, one of the misconceptions about dishwashers is that they use a lot of water, electricity, and detergent, and that they do not need to pre-wash the dishes. I am one of those who thought, "Why bother? If you just wash them and throw them away, you can just be a little more diligent. Why bother?" But then I hit menopause at 50 and my finger joints started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't invest this much in myself~~" When I was selected for the experience group, I was thrilled. I found out that there are also compact sizes that can fit 3-4 people in a small space. The models that are coming out these days have good performance and they say that they clean well even without pre-washing. I guess it's an improvement. But personally, I think pre-washing the dishes is a way to solve the hassle of not having to do the secondary manual work to remove grease or seasoning. The monthly electricity bill for 6 people is 2,000-3,000 won. It can be done for less than 100 won for 4 people, so let's put aside the burden for a moment~ Opening soon~~~~~ Roughly 40cm in width, length, and height. It's a cube shape with a soft curve. Among the components, our spoon is made of wood, so we plan to use it without inserting the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose was not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is an easy way to tighten it by inserting it into the drain hole. When supplying water manually, you must press the power button 'be sure' to supply water to check the water tank alarm sound. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) is said to be suitable for basic washing because the amount of water is small, but it takes 1 hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) 29 minutes. The only regret is that there is no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. You also have to use a 'detergent for washing'. Since it was my first time, I searched and bought a detergent that worked well among the ones I tested. I just put it on a square tray without a spout and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablet, it'll fall to the floor when I close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to be? (It just falls.) When washing larger dishes, you can fold the secret bar to make better use of space, and it has wheels so you don't have to put your hands deep inside, which is convenient. It doesn't make much noise, and I think the force of the spray from below is strong. Hot water comes out when you drain it. It's not enough to burn you, but you have to be careful. I feel like my quality of life has improved since I was freed from the housework of washing dishes. I like how it makes me smile when I see clean dishes. If you feel this way, I'd like to recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be good to use it for 2~3 people in the future. It's a little short on space, and it would be better if a drying function was added separately, not for washing. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

It's a little short on space, and it would be better if a drying function was added separately, not for washing. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

(그냥 떨어지네요 ㅋㅋ) 좀 큰그릇 세척시엔 시크릿바를 접을수 있어 공간활용도 되고 이동바퀴가 있어 깊숙이 손을 넣을 필요도 없이 편합니다. 생활소음정도  크진않고 밑에서 쏘는 힘이 쎈가봐요. 배수때 뜨거운물이 빠져요. 화상입을정도는 아니여도 조심해야겠습니다. 설겆이라는 가사노동에서 해방되면서 맘적으로 삶의 질이 높아진 느낌이랄까... 뽀득뽀득한 그릇을 보니 웃음이 나는게 기부니가 좋아졌어요. 이런 맘이면 식기세척기 추천해드리고 싶네요..  추후-2~3인용으로 사용하면 좋을듯 싶어요. 공간이 살짝 부족하고 세척용도가 아닌 건조기능이 따로 추가가되면 더 좋겠어요 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료로 제공 받아 작성한 구매 후기입니다.

Sentence (English): It's a cube shape with a soft curve.
Comments (English): In fact, one of the misconceptions about dishwashers is that they use a lot of water, electricity, and detergent, and that they do not need to pre-wash the dishes. I am one of those who thought, "Why bother? If you just wash them and throw them away, you can just be a little more diligent. Why bother?" But then I hit menopause at 50 and my finger joints started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't invest this much in myself~~" When I was selected for the experience group, I was thrilled. I found out that there are also compact sizes that can fit 3-4 people in a small space. The models that are coming out these days have good performance and they say that they clean well even without pre-washing. I guess it's an improvement. But personally, I think pre-washing the dishes is a way to solve the hassle of not having to do the secondary manual work to remove grease or seasoning. The monthly electricity bill for 6 people is 2,000-3,000 won. It can be done for less than 100 won for 4 people, so let's put aside the burden for a moment~ Opening soon~~~~~ Roughly 40cm in width, length, and height. It's a cube shape with a soft curve. Among the components, our spoon is made of wood, so we plan to use it without inserting the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose was not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is an easy way to tighten it by inserting it into the drain hole. When supplying water manually, you must press the power button 'be sure' to supply water to check the water tank alarm sound. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) is said to be suitable for basic washing because the amount of water is small, but it takes 1 hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) 29 minutes. The only regret is that there is no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. You also have to use a 'detergent for washing'. Since it was my first time, I searched and bought a detergent that worked well among the ones I tested. I just put it on a square tray without a spout and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablet, it'll fall to the floor when I close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to be? (It just falls.) When washing larger dishes, you can fold the secret bar to make better use of space, and it has wheels so you don't have to put your hands deep inside, which is convenient. It doesn't make much noise, and I think the force of the spray from below is strong. Hot water comes out when you drain it. It's not enough to burn you, but you have to be careful. I feel like my quality of life has improved since I was freed from the housework of washing dishes. I like how it makes me smile when I see clean dishes. If you feel this way, I'd like to recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be good to use it for 2~3 people in the future. It's a little short on space, and it would be better if a drying function was added separately, not for washing. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

The only regret is that there is no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. You also have to use a 'detergent for washing'. Since it was my first time, I searched and bought a detergent that worked well among the ones I tested. I just put it on a square tray without a spout and close the door. When washing larger dishes, you can fold the secret bar to make better use of space, and it has wheels so you don't have to put your hands deep inside, which is convenient. It's a little short on space, and it would be better if a drying function was added separately, not for washing. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

(그냥 떨어지네요 ㅋㅋ) 좀 큰그릇 세척시엔 시크릿바를 접을수 있어 공간활용도 되고 이동바퀴가 있어 깊숙이 손을 넣을 필요도 없이 편합니다. 생활소음정도  크진않고 밑에서 쏘는 힘이 쎈가봐요. 배수때 뜨거운물이 빠져요. 화상입을정도는 아니여도 조심해야겠습니다. 설겆이라는 가사노동에서 해방되면서 맘적으로 삶의 질이 높아진 느낌이랄까... 뽀득뽀득한 그릇을 보니 웃음이 나는게 기부니가 좋아졌어요. 이런 맘이면 식기세척기 추천해드리고 싶네요..  추후-2~3인용으로 사용하면 좋을듯 싶어요. 공간이 살짝 부족하고 세척용도가 아닌 건조기능이 따로 추가가되면 더 좋겠어요 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료로 제공 받아 작성한 구매 후기입니다.

Sentence (English): Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) is said to be suitable for basic washing because the amount of water is small, but it takes 1 hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) 29 minutes.
Comments (English): In fact, one of the misconceptions about dishwashers is that they use a lot of water, electricity, and detergent, and that they do not need to pre-wash the dishes. I am one of those who thought, "Why bother? If you just wash them and throw them away, you can just be a little more diligent. Why bother?" But then I hit menopause at 50 and my finger joints started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't invest this much in myself~~" When I was selected for the experience group, I was thrilled. I found out that there are also compact sizes that can fit 3-4 people in a small space. The models that are coming out these days have good performance and they say that they clean well even without pre-washing. I guess it's an improvement. But personally, I think pre-washing the dishes is a way to solve the hassle of not having to do the secondary manual work to remove grease or seasoning. The monthly electricity bill for 6 people is 2,000-3,000 won. It can be done for less than 100 won for 4 people, so let's put aside the burden for a moment~ Opening soon~~~~~ Roughly 40cm in width, length, and height. It's a cube shape with a soft curve. Among the components, our spoon is made of wood, so we plan to use it without inserting the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose was not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is an easy way to tighten it by inserting it into the drain hole. When supplying water manually, you must press the power button 'be sure' to supply water to check the water tank alarm sound. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) is said to be suitable for basic washing because the amount of water is small, but it takes 1 hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) 29 minutes. The only regret is that there is no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. You also have to use a 'detergent for washing'. Since it was my first time, I searched and bought a detergent that worked well among the ones I tested. I just put it on a square tray without a spout and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablet, it'll fall to the floor when I close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to be? (It just falls.) When washing larger dishes, you can fold the secret bar to make better use of space, and it has wheels so you don't have to put your hands deep inside, which is convenient. It doesn't make much noise, and I think the force of the spray from below is strong. Hot water comes out when you drain it. It's not enough to burn you, but you have to be careful. I feel like my quality of life has improved since I was freed from the housework of washing dishes. I like how it makes me smile when I see clean dishes. If you feel this way, I'd like to recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be good to use it for 2~3 people in the future. It's a little short on space, and it would be better if a drying function was added separately, not for washing. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

When supplying water manually, you must press the power button 'be sure' to supply water to check the water tank alarm sound. But whether it's liquid or tablet, it'll fall to the floor when I close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to be? (It just falls.) When washing larger dishes, you can fold the secret bar to make better use of space, and it has wheels so you don't have to put your hands deep inside, which is convenient. It doesn't make much noise, and I think the force of the spray from below is strong. Hot water comes out when you drain it. It's not enough to burn you, but you have to be careful. I feel like my quality of life has improved since I was freed from the housework of washing dishes. I like how it makes me smile when I see clean dishes. It's a little short on space, and it would be better if a drying function was added separately, not for washing. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.
Comments (Original): 사실상 식기세척기 오해중에 하나가 물,전기,세제 양이 많고 애벌설겆이를 하는데 굳이.. 참말로 그냥 씻어 엎으면되는걸 게을러서 조금만 부지런을 떨면될것을 굳이..왜..라고 생각했던 사람중 한사람이 접니다. 그런데 50에 갱년기가 겹치고 손가락 관절 마디마디가 쑤시기 시작했고 갑자기 인생사 뭐있나..나한테 이정도도 투자못하겠어~~지름신 함 불러내지 할때 체험단에 선정되어 신이 났습니다. 작은공간에 3~4인기준 넘 아담한 사이즈도 있다는걸 알았네요. 요즘 나오는 모델들은 성능도 좋고 애벌설겆이를 안해도 깨끗한 세척이된다고 합니다. 개선이 된거겠죠. 그래도 개인적인 생각으론 기름때나 벌건 양념은 애벌을 해주는게 2차 수작업으로 가지않는 번거로움 해결방법이지 않을까 싶어요. 6인 기준으로 한달 전기요금이 2~3천원 나온대요. 4인기준 한번 돌리는데 백원 미만으로도 나올수 있다니 부담감은 잠시 접어두고~ 개봉박두~~~~~ 대충 가로 세로 높이가 40cm. 부드러운 곡선의 큐브모양이예요. 구성품중에 저흰 수저가 목재여서 수저통은 끼우지않고 사용하려합니다. 모든  식기가 세척에 적합하질않아 확인도 필수. 입수호스는 연결하지않았고 배수호수는(길이145cm정도)배수구멍에 콕끼워 조임새로 쪼는 쉬운 방식입니다. 수동급수시에는 '꼭' 전원버튼을 누른 후 급수를해야 물탱크 알림음 확인할수 있습니다. 작동버튼중에 표준코스(세척65도-헹굼-헹굼70도-건조)가 물의 양이 적고 기본 세척에 적합하다는데 시간이 1시간이나 걸려서 시간이 짧은 쾌속 (세척55도-헹굼-헹굼60도)29분으로 사용해볼까 생각중입니다. 아쉬운건 건조 기능이없어 문을 열어 말려야합니다. 또 '세척전용세제'를 써야된데요. 첨인지라 검색을 해보니 세정제 실험한것중에 성능 좋은걸루 구매했어요.  주입구가 없는 그냥 사각 트레이 모양에  얹고 문을 닫아요. 근데 액상이든 타블렛이든 문을 닫으면 바닥으로 떨어지겠는데 원래가 이런 방식인건가? (그냥 떨어지네요 ㅋㅋ) 좀 큰그릇 세척시엔 시크릿바를 접을수 있어 공간활용도 되고 이동바퀴가 있어 깊숙이 손을 넣을 필요도 없이 편합니다. 생활소음정도  크진않고 밑에서 쏘는 힘이 쎈가봐요. 배수때 뜨거운물이 빠져요. 화상입을정도는 아니여도 조심해야겠습니다. 설겆이라는 가사노동에서 해방되면서 맘적으로 삶의 질이 높아진 느낌이랄까... 뽀득뽀득한 그릇을 보니 웃음이 나는게 기부니가 좋아졌어요. 이런 맘이면 식기세척기 추천해드리고 싶네요..  추후-2~3인용으로 사용하면 좋을듯 싶어요. 공간이 살짝 부족하고 세척용도가 아닌 건조기능이 따로 추가가되면 더 좋겠어요 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료로 제공 받아 작성한 구매 후기입니다.

(그냥 떨어지네요 ㅋㅋ) 좀 큰그릇 세척시엔 시크릿바를 접을수 있어 공간활용도 되고 이동바퀴가 있어 깊숙이 손을 넣을 필요도 없이 편합니다. 생활소음정도  크진않고 밑에서 쏘는 힘이 쎈가봐요. 배수때 뜨거운물이 빠져요. 화상입을정도는 아니여도 조심해야겠습니다. 설겆이라는 가사노동에서 해방되면서 맘적으로 삶의 질이 높아진 느낌이랄까... 뽀득뽀득한 그릇을 보니 웃음이 나는게 기부니가 좋아졌어요. 이런 맘이면 식기세척기 추천해드리고 싶네요..  추후-2~3인용으로 사용하면 좋을듯 싶어요. 공간이 살짝 부족하고 세척용도가 아닌 건조기능이 따로 추가가되면 더 좋겠어요 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료로 제공 받아 작성한 구매 후기입니다.

Sentence (English): I just put it on a square tray without a spout and close the door.
Comments (English): In fact, one of the misconceptions about dishwashers is that they use a lot of water, electricity, and detergent, and that they do not need to pre-wash the dishes. I am one of those who thought, "Why bother? If you just wash them and throw them away, you can just be a little more diligent. Why bother?" But then I hit menopause at 50 and my finger joints started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't invest this much in myself~~" When I was selected for the experience group, I was thrilled. I found out that there are also compact sizes that can fit 3-4 people in a small space. The models that are coming out these days have good performance and they say that they clean well even without pre-washing. I guess it's an improvement. But personally, I think pre-washing the dishes is a way to solve the hassle of not having to do the secondary manual work to remove grease or seasoning. The monthly electricity bill for 6 people is 2,000-3,000 won. It can be done for less than 100 won for 4 people, so let's put aside the burden for a moment~ Opening soon~~~~~ Roughly 40cm in width, length, and height. It's a cube shape with a soft curve. Among the components, our spoon is made of wood, so we plan to use it without inserting the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose was not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is an easy way to tighten it by inserting it into the drain hole. When supplying water manually, you must press the power button 'be sure' to supply water to check the water tank alarm sound. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) is said to be suitable for basic washing because the amount of water is small, but it takes 1 hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) 29 minutes. The only regret is that there is no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. You also have to use a 'detergent for washing'. Since it was my first time, I searched and bought a detergent that worked well among the ones I tested. I just put it on a square tray without a spout and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablet, it'll fall to the floor when I close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to be? (It just falls.) When washing larger dishes, you can fold the secret bar to make better use of space, and it has wheels so you don't have to put your hands deep inside, which is convenient. It doesn't make much noise, and I think the force of the spray from below is strong. Hot water comes out when you drain it. It's not enough to burn you, but you have to be careful. I feel like my quality of life has improved since I was freed from the housework of washing dishes. I like how it makes me smile when I see clean dishes. If you feel this way, I'd like to recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be good to use it for 2~3 people in the future. It's a little short on space, and it would be better if a drying function was added separately, not for washing. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Sentence (English): When washing larger dishes, you can fold the secret bar to make better use of space, and it has wheels so you don't have to put your hands deep inside, which is convenient.
Comments (English): In fact, one of the misconceptions about dishwashers is that they use a lot of water, electricity, and detergent, and that they do not need to pre-wash the dishes. I am one of those who thought, "Why bother? If you just wash them and throw them away, you can just be a little more diligent. Why bother?" But then I hit menopause at 50 and my finger joints started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't invest this much in myself~~" When I was selected for the experience group, I was thrilled. I found out that there are also compact sizes that can fit 3-4 people in a small space. The models that are coming out these days have good performance and they say that they clean well even without pre-washing. I guess it's an improvement. But personally, I think pre-washing the dishes is a way to solve the hassle of not having to do the secondary manual work to remove grease or seasoning. The monthly electricity bill for 6 people is 2,000-3,000 won. It can be done for less than 100 won for 4 people, so let's put aside the burden for a moment~ Opening soon~~~~~ Roughly 40cm in width, length, and height. It's a cube shape with a soft curve. Among the components, our spoon is made of wood, so we plan to use it without inserting the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose was not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is an easy way to tighten it by inserting it into the drain hole. When supplying water manually, you must press the power button 'be sure' to supply water to check the water tank alarm sound. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) is said to be suitable for basic washing because the amount of water is small, but it takes 1 hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) 29 minutes. The only regret is that there is no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. You also have to use a 'detergent for washing'. Since it was my first time, I searched and bought a detergent that worked well among the ones I tested. I just put it on a square tray without a spout and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablet, it'll fall to the floor when I close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to be? (It just falls.) When washing larger dishes, you can fold the secret bar to make better use of space, and it has wheels so you don't have to put your hands deep inside, which is convenient. It doesn't make much noise, and I think the force of the spray from below is strong. Hot water comes out when you drain it. It's not enough to burn you, but you have to be careful. I feel like my quality of life has improved since I was freed from the housework of washing dishes. I like how it makes me smile when I see clean dishes. If you feel this way, I'd like to recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be good to use it for 2~3 people in the future. It's a little short on space, and it would be better if a drying function was added separately, not for washing. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Comments (English): In fact, one of the misconceptions about dishwashers is that they use a lot of water, electricity, and detergent, and that they do not need to pre-wash the dishes. I am one of those who thought, "Why bother? If you just wash them and throw them away, you can just be a little more diligent. Why bother?" But then I hit menopause at 50 and my finger joints started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't invest this much in myself~~" When I was selected for the experience group, I was thrilled. I found out that there are also compact sizes that can fit 3-4 people in a small space. The models that are coming out these days have good performance and they say that they clean well even without pre-washing. I guess it's an improvement. But personally, I think pre-washing the dishes is a way to solve the hassle of not having to do the secondary manual work to remove grease or seasoning. The monthly electricity bill for 6 people is 2,000-3,000 won. It can be done for less than 100 won for 4 people, so let's put aside the burden for a moment~ Opening soon~~~~~ Roughly 40cm in width, length, and height. It's a cube shape with a soft curve. Among the components, our spoon is made of wood, so we plan to use it without inserting the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose was not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is an easy way to tighten it by inserting it into the drain hole. When supplying water manually, you must press the power button 'be sure' to supply water to check the water tank alarm sound. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) is said to be suitable for basic washing because the amount of water is small, but it takes 1 hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) 29 minutes. The only regret is that there is no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. You also have to use a 'detergent for washing'. Since it was my first time, I searched and bought a detergent that worked well among the ones I tested. I just put it on a square tray without a spout and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablet, it'll fall to the floor when I close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to be? (It just falls.) When washing larger dishes, you can fold the secret bar to make better use of space, and it has wheels so you don't have to put your hands deep inside, which is convenient. It doesn't make much noise, and I think the force of the spray from below is strong. Hot water comes out when you drain it. It's not enough to burn you, but you have to be careful. I feel like my quality of life has improved since I was freed from the housework of washing dishes. I like how it makes me smile when I see clean dishes. If you feel this way, I'd like to recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be good to use it for 2~3 people in the future. It's a little short on space, and it would be better if a drying function was added separately, not for washing. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Comments (English): In fact, one of the misconceptions about dishwashers is that they use a lot of water, electricity, and detergent, and that they do not need to pre-wash the dishes. I am one of those who thought, "Why bother? If you just wash them and throw them away, you can just be a little more diligent. Why bother?" But then I hit menopause at 50 and my finger joints started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't invest this much in myself~~" When I was selected for the experience group, I was thrilled. I found out that there are also compact sizes that can fit 3-4 people in a small space. The models that are coming out these days have good performance and they say that they clean well even without pre-washing. I guess it's an improvement. But personally, I think pre-washing the dishes is a way to solve the hassle of not having to do the secondary manual work to remove grease or seasoning. The monthly electricity bill for 6 people is 2,000-3,000 won. It can be done for less than 100 won for 4 people, so let's put aside the burden for a moment~ Opening soon~~~~~ Roughly 40cm in width, length, and height. It's a cube shape with a soft curve. Among the components, our spoon is made of wood, so we plan to use it without inserting the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose was not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is an easy way to tighten it by inserting it into the drain hole. When supplying water manually, you must press the power button 'be sure' to supply water to check the water tank alarm sound. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) is said to be suitable for basic washing because the amount of water is small, but it takes 1 hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) 29 minutes. The only regret is that there is no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. You also have to use a 'detergent for washing'. Since it was my first time, I searched and bought a detergent that worked well among the ones I tested. I just put it on a square tray without a spout and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablet, it'll fall to the floor when I close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to be? (It just falls.) When washing larger dishes, you can fold the secret bar to make better use of space, and it has wheels so you don't have to put your hands deep inside, which is convenient. It doesn't make much noise, and I think the force of the spray from below is strong. Hot water comes out when you drain it. It's not enough to burn you, but you have to be careful. I feel like my quality of life has improved since I was freed from the housework of washing dishes. I like how it makes me smile when I see clean dishes. If you feel this way, I'd like to recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be good to use it for 2~3 people in the future. Sentence (English): I originally had an old LG dishwasher that belonged to my aunt.
Comments (English): [ Aunt who improves the quality of life ] || ---------------- || I originally had an old LG dishwasher that belonged to my aunt. But then I moved and had to replace it. I bought it during a sale, so the price was reasonable. My old dishwasher had two tiers and a separate cutlery drawer, but this one has three tiers, so I can wash spoons, chopsticks, knives, and other utensils separately in the top tier, which is nice. The light beige color goes well with my white kitchen, but the lack of white is a bit disappointing. (I asked the technician about color changes upon delivery, but he said this model doesn't come in white, so changing the panel is not possible.) It's a convenient model with a high-temperature drying function and an automatic door opening. My overall impression: While it has a high-temperature drying function, water still collects in the dents when I turn dishes upside down. I slightly regretted buying a model with a hot air drying function from the beginning. And since the hot air drying model had a white panel, there was only about a 30% difference when I bought it, but I regret not buying the higher-end model after using it for 5 years. It is the best value for money, but if I were to buy it again, I think I would pay more and buy the higher-end model.
