Sentence (English): I'm a homebody living alone for 8 years.
Comments (English): [ A must-have for single-person households ] || ---------------- || I'm a homebody living alone for 8 years. I love cooking and inviting people over, but the hardest part of it is always washing the dishes. I debated for a while before finally splurging, and I love it so much that I regret not buying it sooner. With coupons and card discounts, it was nearly 100,000 won cheaper than the lowest price on Naver. So, single-person households shouldn't hesitate to buy it. # Pros. I assume everyone knows about the automatic door opening, so I'll skip that part. What I'm most satisfied with is the single-story structure! You might think a 6-person capacity is too small and you can't fit many dishes, but because of the single-story design, you can fit large pots without any problems. I even managed to fit a pot for boiling pasta! At this level, I think you could say almost anything fits, except for a stockpot. Also, I'm satisfied because the noise level is lower than I expected. Especially when it's drying, I don't hear a sound at all, so I wondered if it was even running (though it was working perfectly fine). # Cons. It's a shame that drilling a hole is required to connect the water supply hose. That is something to be concerned about if you are renting on a lease or monthly basis. The drain hose is quite thick, but instead of drilling a hole, it is installed to run directly into the sink. It bothered me a lot at first, but it was fine once I got used to it. Also, the product is quite a bit larger than I expected, so it might be a bit overwhelming for small homes. # This is how I use it. I use solid tablet detergent. Although the instructions say to cut it in half for a 6-person set, putting in just a quarter is enough. Detergent isn't cheap, so let's save money together.

All the utensils and plates used for cooking or eating ] || ---------------- || I have been using the dishwasher for a month. To start with the good things, the stress of washing dishes has been reduced a lot. I didn't know it would be this good either. Whether you're cooking or eating, you can just put away all the utensils and plates, so it's very convenient. The automatic door opening feature is also really nice. However, if the bowl has a deep groove on the top when turned over, the water will not dry out over time. So after I finish washing them, I turn them over one by one. Usually everything is dry inside. It will dry completely after a while. The unfortunate thing is that there are more dishes that cannot be put in the dishwasher than expected (plastic, coated pans, rice cooker inner pot, spoons and forks with handles, etc.) and sometimes there are dishes/pots that are difficult to wash. I don't know why, but it always seemed like the kid who couldn't do it kept failing. When you take it out, you can see traces of detergent and food residue. So, I check it carefully every time I take it out, but I think it's not a big deal compared to the stress of washing dishes. People who are considering whether or not to buy a dishwasher for the first time may have concerns about cleaning power, parts that need to be rinsed beforehand, drying problems, fishy water smell, etc. Despite all the problems, I strongly recommend it. It's really good in terms of time, stamina, and emotions(?). Don't buy one that fits 6 people, but be sure to buy the larger one. (Even if you are a single-person household, if you use a lot of things while cooking, it will not be enough for 6 people.) Buy dishwasher-safe plates, cutlery, cooking utensils, and pots/pans to use them comfortably.

All the utensils and plates used for cooking or eating ] || ---------------- || I have been using the dishwasher for a month. To start with the good things, the stress of washing dishes has been reduced a lot. I didn't know it would be this good either. Whether you're cooking or eating, you can just put away all the utensils and plates, so it's very convenient. The automatic door opening feature is also really nice. However, if the bowl has a deep groove on the top when turned over, the water will not dry out over time. So after I finish washing them, I turn them over one by one. Usually everything is dry inside. It will dry completely after a while. The unfortunate thing is that there are more dishes that cannot be put in the dishwasher than expected (plastic, coated pans, rice cooker inner pot, spoons and forks with handles, etc.) and sometimes there are dishes/pots that are difficult to wash. I don't know why, but it always seemed like the kid who couldn't do it kept failing. When you take it out, you can see traces of detergent and food residue. So, I check it carefully every time I take it out, but I think it's not a big deal compared to the stress of washing dishes. People who are considering whether or not to buy a dishwasher for the first time may have concerns about cleaning power, parts that need to be rinsed beforehand, drying problems, fishy water smell, etc. Despite all the problems, I strongly recommend it. It's really good in terms of time, stamina, and emotions(?). Don't buy one that fits 6 people, but be sure to buy the larger one. (Even if you are a single-person household, if you use a lot of things while cooking, it will not be enough for 6 people.) To start with the good things, the stress of washing dishes has been reduced a lot. I didn't know it would be this good either. Whether you're cooking or eating, you can just put away all the utensils and plates, so it's very convenient. The automatic door opening feature is also really nice. However, if the bowl has a deep groove on the top when turned over, the water will not dry out over time. So after I finish washing them, I turn them over one by one. Usually everything is dry inside. It will dry completely after a while. The unfortunate thing is that there are more dishes that cannot be put in the dishwasher than expected (plastic, coated pans, rice cooker inner pot, spoons and forks with handles, etc.) and sometimes there are dishes/pots that are difficult to wash. I don't know why, but it always seemed like the kid who couldn't do it kept failing. When you take it out, you can see traces of detergent and food residue. So, I check it carefully every time I take it out, but I think it's not a big deal compared to the stress of washing dishes. People who are considering whether or not to buy a dishwasher for the first time may have concerns about cleaning power, parts that need to be rinsed beforehand, drying problems, fishy water smell, etc. Despite all the problems, I strongly recommend it. It's really good in terms of time, stamina, and emotions(?). Don't buy one that fits 6 people, but be sure to buy the larger one. (Even if you are a single-person household, if you use a lot of things while cooking, it will not be enough for 6 people.) All the utensils and plates used for cooking or eating ] || ---------------- || I have been using the dishwasher for a month. To start with the good things, the stress of washing dishes has been reduced a lot. I didn't know it would be this good either. Whether you're cooking or eating, you can just put away all the utensils and plates, so it's very convenient. The automatic door opening feature is also really nice. However, if the bowl has a deep groove on the top when turned over, the water will not dry out over time. So after I finish washing them, I turn them over one by one. Usually everything is dry inside. It will dry completely after a while. The unfortunate thing is that there are more dishes that cannot be put in the dishwasher than expected (plastic, coated pans, rice cooker inner pot, spoons and forks with handles, etc.) and sometimes there are dishes/pots that are difficult to wash. I don't know why, but it always seemed like the kid who couldn't do it kept failing. When you take it out, you can see traces of detergent and food residue. So, I check it carefully every time I take it out, but I think it's not a big deal compared to the stress of washing dishes. People who are considering whether or not to buy a dishwasher for the first time may have concerns about cleaning power, parts that need to be rinsed beforehand, drying problems, fishy water smell, etc. Despite all the problems, I strongly recommend it. It's really good in terms of time, stamina, and emotions(?). Don't buy one that fits 6 people, but be sure to buy the larger one. (Even if you are a single-person household, if you use a lot of things while cooking, it will not be enough for 6 people.) Sentence (English): I love this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Great Dishwasher, A Couple Appearance Dislikes ] || ---------------- || I love this dishwasher. It gets my dishes super clean and dry. It has two wash levels, top and bottom. It's got adjustable racks. An easy to clean filter. The cycles for a complete sanitation take way longer than I thought they would. but with one load a day, it's not something you even notice, especially with how quiet this thing is. I love the sanitation cycle and the dry boost is cool because it dries the dishes completely. The only thing I did not like about this dishwasher is there is no GE emblem on the front of it like all my other GE appliances. (I ended up buying a spare emblem from a parts website for the stainless refrigerator and stuck it on there where I thought it looked right lol). As well, there's a gap on the bottom of the dishwasher where I thought there would be some kind of cover to match my cabinets where they meet the floor so I don't see underneath the dishwasher, instead, I just see the screw bolt things that level it out. For those considering this dishwasher, just throwing this out here, My dishwasher was hardwired and the installation company required a GFCI outlet for it to plug into after they use a kit to wire it up to a plug. Though my outlet is on a GFCI circuit alongside a GFCI and Arc protection breaker, They refused to plug it into the outlet that's under my sink for my garbage disposal, and instead made me purchase a GFCI outlet box that they mounted inside my cabinet. It wasn't that expensive but it kind of took me back a bit. I wasn't about to postpone the installation and have an electrician do it instead.

The unit cleans ok but the sprayer arms seem to hold water after the cycle is over. No matter what dry setting I use (sani dry, heated dry, extended dry, heated & extended) the dishes always come out with some level of moisture on them. Even though the tub is stainless steel the mid sprayer arm is plastic and leaks onto the dishes below and bottom after the cycle is completed, leaving water that eventually evaporates onto the dishes. Even if the arm didn't leak the dishes never seem to get completely dry. It's become extremely tiresome after the past year to constantly have to towel dry everything when emptying the unit.

Comments (English): [ Recommended for small households without installation ] || ---------------- || I needed a dishwasher after moving. I hope this helps you decide if you want to buy one after actually using it. Please read this, even though it's a bit long. I'll be honest. Size. I thought it would be big because it said it was for 2-3 people. It's actually quite large. I thought it was about the size of a microwave, but the photos don't really do it justice. The manual says it's 43.5" high, 42" wide, and 43.5" deep. It weighs 14kg. I measured it with a tape measure and it's 43.5" high, 41" wide, and 41" deep. There may be a 1-2 cm margin of error depending on who measures. The drain line is long, so you can cut it to fit your needs. 2 people. I'm a couple with no children. We're both big eaters, so we mostly use large plates, bowls, and large cups. This seems perfect for a family of two. It includes 4 soup bowls, side dish plates, 3-4 spoons, chopsticks, and a cup. The manual says to arrange the bowls straight, but I prefer to place them diagonally. Because it sprays water from above and below, the entire bowl is touched, making it easy to clean. Good point. I mostly cook at home, and the biggest headache was the cups. I used to prioritize the cups before washing the dishes, but they had a distinct fishy smell. Sometimes, even after rinsing them with hot water, the smell persists. Next came the oily dishes and plates, but the result was no longer the squeaky, greasy smell of the bowls and cups. It's fun to fill them up, layer by layer, like playing Tetris. It's also easy to install because it's non-perforated. Overall: It's a bit of a hassle to add water one by one, but my husband and I, a family of two who frequently cook at home and are sensitive to odors, were satisfied with it because it eliminated the fishy smell from the oily water and cups. The price is reasonable at 200,000 won, and the non-perforated installation makes it easy to access. I placed it in the front, but after using it, I moved it to the side. I'm going to try rotating it again. It's great for cooking, but washing dishes is a hassle. Important. (Do not simply run it with food in it. You must remove any remaining food before use to avoid clogging.) This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Comments (English): [ Recommended for small households without installation ] || ---------------- || I needed a dishwasher after moving. I hope this helps you decide if you want to buy one after actually using it. Please read this, even though it's a bit long. I'll be honest. Size. I thought it would be big because it said it was for 2-3 people. It's actually quite large. I thought it was about the size of a microwave, but the photos don't really do it justice. The manual says it's 43.5" high, 42" wide, and 43.5" deep. It weighs 14kg. I measured it with a tape measure and it's 43.5" high, 41" wide, and 41" deep. There may be a 1-2 cm margin of error depending on who measures. The drain line is long, so you can cut it to fit your needs. 2 people. I'm a couple with no children. We're both big eaters, so we mostly use large plates, bowls, and large cups. This seems perfect for a family of two. It includes 4 soup bowls, side dish plates, 3-4 spoons, chopsticks, and a cup. The manual says to arrange the bowls straight, but I prefer to place them diagonally. Because it sprays water from above and below, the entire bowl is touched, making it easy to clean. Good point. I mostly cook at home, and the biggest headache was the cups. I used to prioritize the cups before washing the dishes, but they had a distinct fishy smell. Sometimes, even after rinsing them with hot water, the smell persists. Next came the oily dishes and plates, but the result was no longer the squeaky, greasy smell of the bowls and cups. It's fun to fill them up, layer by layer, like playing Tetris. It's also easy to install because it's non-perforated. Overall: It's a bit of a hassle to add water one by one, but my husband and I, a family of two who frequently cook at home and are sensitive to odors, were satisfied with it because it eliminated the fishy smell from the oily water and cups. The price is reasonable at 200,000 won, and the non-perforated installation makes it easy to access. I placed it in the front, but after using it, I moved it to the side. I'm going to try rotating it again. It's great for cooking, but washing dishes is a hassle. Important. (Do not simply run it with food in it. You must remove any remaining food before use to avoid clogging.) This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

It's ease of operation, with it's simple set-up of buttons that display the length of each cycle, make it a pleasure to use. I find it quick and easy to put in a detergent tab, click it shut, and add rinse agent if needed. The dishwasher works well with the rinse aid and even gives a reminder to add it when it runs out. I like the ease of loading the dishwasher, the dinner dishes line up nicely on the bottom, along with space for pots and pans, and baskets for silverware. The top works well for cups, mugs and bowls, and even has pieces that pull down to load stemware and keep it secure. This dishwasher also includes a top tray for cutlery and lids, which I don't use, but is a nice option for a consumer who needs more room for these items. A bonus is that this dishwasher runs so quietly that you don't even know it's running. Also, the stainless steel color matches with the other appliances in my kitchen. Pricewise, I feel this dishwasher is more affordable than other options of its kind. I would definitely recommend this product to anyone looking for a reliable and affordable dishwasher for their kitchen.

Sentence (English): Pros: Cleans great.
Comments (English): Pros: Cleans great. I run my dishwasher every two to three days. I don't have to pre-rinse, but I do a bit on really gooey things when I'm not going to run it that day. The third rack is great; so handy. The top rack is versatile; it seems I can always squeeze in one more item. I like the flatware caddy; it's also versatile. I can put little things in, close the lid, and not lose anything. It seems tedious to load each piece of flatware, but it works great. I group each type together when I load, so everything is already sorted when I put away the clean things. The disadvantage is you can't unload by the handles. Wash your hands first! I can put little things in, close the lid, and not lose anything. It seems tedious to load each piece of flatware, but it works great. I group each type together when I load, so everything is already sorted when I put away the clean things. The disadvantage is you can't unload by the handles. Wash your hands first! The adjustable top rack is a nice feature, but it's a little tricky to do, especially if you've already put things (especially breakable and/or heavy things) in the rack. It sings a little tune when the cycle is finished. Always makes me laugh.Cons: The dishwasher is designed to accommodate eight place settings of dishes with the plates on the lower level with their edges overlapping plus a couple serving bowls. I have stoneware - the plates are thick and there's no way they will load like that. I would never load my china that closely. We use a lot of bowls. The flat soup bowls load as do plates, but fruit bowls have to go on the upper or third rack and there's only room for six cereal bowls on the front end of the lower rack plus one or two on the side. I end up with an empty space EVERY time I run a load.I don't like the dark interior. Light would be nice, but that's certainly not a deal breaker.All in all, I'm very pleased.

Sentence (English): Replaced my 12 year old GE monogram dishwasher with this model.
Comments (English): [ Quiet but that's about all I like….  ] || ---------------- || Replaced my 12 year old GE monogram dishwasher with this model. The first week I had this dishwasher, the control board freaked out so we had to crawl under the sink to unplug the dishwasher. After it reset, it has worked since but I hope that is not an ongoing issue. I do think the dishwasher is extremely quiet and in theory, the extra glass jets might be useful someday. I thought I would enjoy the small top rack but nothing really fits well or it has water standing on it after a wash. Really miss the stem wear rack in my old dishwasher. It was great for small items. There are several things I definitely don't like about this dishwasher. The utensil basket cannot be moved to a different location because of the extra cleaning jets under it. My sink is on the opposite side of the basket so it would be better if I could move the basket to the other side of the bottom rack. This location also impedes placing cookie sheets or skillets on the outsides of the bottom rack. Only one side is available unless you remove the utensil basket. I do not like having to push start twice to begin a load. You have to turn the unit on every time and then push start and shut the door within 4 seconds. It seems to be quite touchy so I have to bend over and listen for the water to be certain it begins to wash. I like the washing/drying/clean screen but even if you barely open the door to grab a glass, it resets the screen to blank. The door should be opened at least halfway down before this screen removes the clean notification. There is also not a real track for the bottom rack so when you roll it back inside, the plates will roll out of place. This is quite annoying. Not sure what the point of the fingerprint free stainless is since the button panel is the worst to get fingerprints on than any dishwasher I have ever had. Maybe use fingerprint free on places used with your fingers. Also, the dishwasher does not have a light inside. The best part of this unit is how quiet it is and there are several worst but in summary, it just doesn't hold as much as my old GE Monogram and is a bit awkward to use.

My sink is on the opposite side of the basket so it would be better if I could move the basket to the other side of the bottom rack. This location also impedes placing cookie sheets or skillets on the outsides of the bottom rack. Only one side is available unless you remove the utensil basket. I do not like having to push start twice to begin a load. You have to turn the unit on every time and then push start and shut the door within 4 seconds. It seems to be quite touchy so I have to bend over and listen for the water to be certain it begins to wash. I like the washing/drying/clean screen but even if you barely open the door to grab a glass, it resets the screen to blank. The door should be opened at least halfway down before this screen removes the clean notification. There is also not a real track for the bottom rack so when you roll it back inside, the plates will roll out of place. This is quite annoying. Not sure what the point of the fingerprint free stainless is since the button panel is the worst to get fingerprints on than any dishwasher I have ever had. Maybe use fingerprint free on places used with your fingers. Also, the dishwasher does not have a light inside. The best part of this unit is how quiet it is and there are several worst but in summary, it just doesn’t hold as much as my old GE Monogram and is a bit awkward to use.

Sentence (English): My 15 year old Kitchenaid needed to be replaced.
Comments (English): [ Cleans great and very quiet. Well built. ] || ---------------- || My 15 year old Kitchenaid needed to be replaced. It was a good machine but was not cleaning as well as it should so I replaced it with a similar model. I wanted the third rack, stainless interior and a quiet machine. I also saw that the water wands were stainless instead of plastic like on some other brands. Pros: My new machine is quiet and cleans very well - even peanut butter on knives! I like the configuration of the top rack. The middle and bottom racks slide out easily and hold a lot. the rinse aid dispenser holds a lot of liquid. Front panel stays fingerprint free. I use the “ProWash” cycle most of the time and dishes are 99% dry which is fine with me but I have used the ProDry and everything was 100% dry …but I think the fan stays in until I open the door to unload machine.The “self clean” feature is great. Not having to clean out “trap” is a great feature. Cons: the light that shines on the floor when dishes are clean is very hard to see on my light beige tile floor especially if lights are on. Would rather have the small button on top of door that lit up a color when done however the display does say “clean”. The top controls are EXTRA sensitive to the touch when opening door requiring me to “cancel” a lot! I liked the sleek look of no door handle but now think it would have been better to have for opening and closing the door. I am slowly getting used to opening the door and not setting off controls! I use dishwasher pods and the holder is a bit small and the plastic latch seems a bit cheap and not easy to close. I think I can hear when it opens in the cycle. I also think the light in the interior might have been a plus which is not on my model. All in all, I am very happy with this well built dishwasher and its performance. I would definitely recommend it to a friend.

Sentence (English): My 15 year old Kitchenaid needed to be replaced.
Comments (English): [ Cleans great and very quiet. Well built. ] || ---------------- || My 15 year old Kitchenaid needed to be replaced. It was a good machine but was not cleaning as well as it should so I replaced it with a similar model. I wanted the third rack, stainless interior and a quiet machine. I also saw that the water wands were stainless instead of plastic like on some other brands. Pros: My new machine is quiet and cleans very well - even peanut butter on knives! I like the configuration of the top rack. The middle and bottom racks slide out easily and hold a lot. the rinse aid dispenser holds a lot of liquid. Front panel stays fingerprint free. I use the "ProWash" cycle most of the time and dishes are 99% dry which is fine with me but I have used the ProDry and everything was 100% dry …but I think the fan stays in until I open the door to unload machine.The "self clean" feature is great. Not having to clean out "trap" is a great feature. Cons: the light that shines on the floor when dishes are clean is very hard to see on my light beige tile floor especially if lights are on. Would rather have the small button on top of door that lit up a color when done however the display does say "clean". The top controls are EXTRA sensitive to the touch when opening door requiring me to "cancel" a lot! I liked the sleek look of no door handle but now think it would have been better to have for opening and closing the door. I am slowly getting used to opening the door and not setting off controls! I use dishwasher pods and the holder is a bit small and the plastic latch seems a bit cheap and not easy to close. I think I can hear when it opens in the cycle. I also think the light in the interior might have been a plus which is not on my model. All in all, I am very happy with this well built dishwasher and its performance. I would definitely recommend it to a friend.

Sentence (English): Our new house isn't very big, so we didn't have a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Worrying only delays your purchase! ] || ---------------- || Our new house isn't very big, so we didn't have a dishwasher. Even if we don't cook much at home, small plates and cups pile up, and if we're not paying attention, the dishes pile up. Because our kitchen isn't very spacious, we looked for a small dishwasher and purchased one. The installation was so simple that even a woman could do it herself. The bottom-mounted water tank is a godsend. It holds a little over 5 liters of water, and the bottom-mounted tank makes it incredibly convenient to fill. Assuming the water is supplied from the top, it seems like spilling it while refilling could create a mess. This dishwasher uses less water than I would if I were doing my own dishes. I highly recommend it. It's quite noisy, perhaps because our house is small. It's like washing dishes by hand with the water running at full power, but for over an hour. Sentence (English): Purchased online from HD mid-September '23.
Comments (English): Purchased online from HD mid-September '23. Coming from a previous KA dishwasher, we expect the best right out of the gate.SO, the pros:Love the towel bar, the print-free SS is def an improvement, the extra third rack is surprisingly helpful (love it now), it holds a lot of dishes especially with the options of moving the middle rack up or down, the dishes are squeaky clean (almost silky) and dry (we use ProWash, Hi Temp Wash, Sani Rinse, Heated dry and Extended Heat Dry).the Cons:IF you are coming from another KA, this model may not seem as quiet as the reviewers claim. While this model is VERY quiet, the model that we just replaced could not be heard. Next, the machine cavity sits lower than our previous model. I am 5'2" and it seems low to me, so it may seem very low to an individual who is taller.Please note that many reviews stated that their washer left dishes soaked; after two test cycles, ours were clean but also wet. Once we filled the rinse aid, however, all dishes are dry.There were also reviews stating that glasses were tipping over in the middle rack but we have not had any issues with that, nor with dinner plates not fitting on the bottom rack.Buy with confidence!

Sentence (English): Purchased Dishwasher Model: SHPM78Z55N/22 Delivered by Home Depot on 8/21/2023 1.
Comments (English): [ Works well, but.  ] || ---------------- || Purchased Dishwasher Model: SHPM78Z55N/22 Delivered by Home Depot on 8/21/2023 1. One of the featured I liked was the LED display, labeled “CYCLE STATUS”, that I was told by Home Depot salesperson, will display the remaining time to the end of the cycle (see Home Depot Display photo). At our request, the dishwasher was mounted exposing 90% of the upper control panel (photo attached), so that we would be able to see the remaining cycle time or, in case something would not sound right or any other reason, we would be able to pause on cancel the cycle before opening the door without getting sprayed all over. While running the dishwasher we found out that the display is off during the cycle. I understand that some people prefer to have their dishwasher flush mounted with their cabinets. I would prefer to have the ability to stop or cancel the cycle before it is completed? When is the display showing “CYCLE STATUS”? 2. It must be “in style” to have a Third Rack for cooking utensils – What a waste of space! – We removed ours on the second day. 3. The Lower Rack Silverware Basket looks and feels like a children toy! Limited capacity and you must align the silverware to fit into the slots (or flip the guide). We were lucky to save our old dishwasher basket and fit it onto the lower tray. 4. Lower tray configuration leaves a lot of unutilized space for our use - I wish we had a choice of different configuration. 5. Cleaning and drying works well and very quiet.

To be honest, when I first started living alone, I had a fantasy about cooking while living alone, so I cooked a lot of things. But as most people who live alone know, the kitchen is really small. I can't cook fancy meals, and even if I do, I have to keep washing dishes and cleaning up while cooking because there is no space. I wash them in the morning and evening, and I do it every day before going to work and after work, so it's become a habit, but sometimes I just think about buying a dishwasher. That's how I ended up ordering a dishwasher, but I felt that I didn't necessarily need a 6-person dishwasher because I only have to wash the cats' dishes. I heard that a 3-person dishwasher is small and doesn't fit a big pot, but I only need to put small dishes in, so this is perfect! I thought that my choice was right! The dishes fit well. 3. The box was so big that it didn't fit in my front door. I had installed a door to the bathroom, so the width wasn't even long enough. So I ended up taking the dishwasher out of the house and bringing it into the house. I was worried because it weighed 14kg, but it was really heavy. But a woman can lift it by herself! At first, I thought it was a detergent, so I was a little impressed, but it's too bad. The inside isn't that big, but I think I can fit small dishes, so I'm very satisfied. It's annoying to have to wash and put the dishes in, but if you put them in, they'll dry out on their own, so I'll just wash them and put them in and take them out the next day. I'm working, so I'm too tired to do everything on weekdays. I'll install it over the weekend and write a more detailed review. 4. Conclusion: I was surprised because it was much bigger than I thought! People who live alone but don't cook at home often, and who don't mind washing large pots and frying pans when cooking but would like to at least wash the dishes! Or people who have pets at home, it would be good to use it. Comments (English): [ When it's working, it works fine ] || ---------------- || Too bad, I was so looking forward to this dishwasher. After using it only twice however, the "Normal" and "Tough" functions were not responding on the touchpad. The only way I can get them to work is before each wash, I have to throw the breaker and cut power to the dishwasher for 30 seconds. After doing that, the "Normal" and "Tough" functions will respond but only for one wash. Next time I have to do it all over again.To make matters worse, after calling customer service they scheduled a repair with a company who did not show up and couldn't be reached via the contact number. After sitting at home for four hours waiting for the repair technician, I called KitchenAid customer service again only to be told that the repair appointment had been cancelled because KitchenAid no longer used that vendor. NO ONE TOLD ME! They then scheduled another appointment with another repair service for the next day. I then received a text from that repair company letting me know they actually were not available during the day and time KitchenAid had scheduled but would reschedule for the next week. They showed up today on time but had been given the wrong repair information by KitchenAid so they did not have the proper parts to fix my dishwasher. The repair technician then looked up the part, found that it is currently out of stock, and will have to call me back when the part finally becomes available in the future to do the repair. This is all for a dishwasher that is now 3 weeks old! I feel good business practice would be for KitchenAid to offer me a $100 (or more) rebate or a free extended 2-3 year warranty in light of all of this.

Sentence (English): When I moved into a new house, I looked into buying a dishwasher.
Comments (English): When I moved into a new house, I looked into buying a dishwasher. I was initially looking at a six-person model, but human greed is endless. Bewildered by the "bigger the better" adage, I settled on a 12-person model. For a family of three, a 12-person model seemed more than enough. There are more expensive dishwashers with hot air dryers, but they're expensive and take more time. So, I looked into a dishwasher with only basic features and ended up buying this one. We set a date, and the LG technician came, installed it, and explained everything to me. He told me to clean it with salt every two months, and to clean other parts once a month. It seemed like a lot more work than I expected, so I wondered if I'd made a bad purchase. But after I finished loading all my dinner dishes, I realized it was still convenient. (You can still put food in it, but it's better to soak it in water and leave it clean. I read somewhere that if you don't, food will collect at the bottom, making cleaning more difficult.) First, there's space for utensils, chopsticks, and tongs. The second and third compartments are also spacious, so pots can fit easily. There are separate compartments for solid and powder detergents. I included a photo of the solid detergent compartment in my review. On default mode, it runs for about 55 minutes and the door opens automatically, but it opens only slightly, so manually opening it seems to be the key to proper drying. Prices on Coupang change daily, so unless you're in a hurry, put it in your cart and buy it on the cheapest day with a strong credit card discount. A tip: I had a moving date, so I bought it in advance. Then, I saw a cheaper price in the middle of the process. I canceled the first item and repurchased the cheaper one. I was able to cancel with two days left, so I exclaimed, "Oh, Coupang!" Also, my sink is a bit high, so I had to reinforce the upper part for 30,000 won. I asked if they wanted to reinforce the lower part where the sink rises, but they said they wouldn't, because the lower part is hard to see and the door is always open. No one wants to look under my dishwasher, so I'd rather it be flat. This was a review of my aunt's dishwasher purchase with her own money!

There are more expensive dishwashers with hot air dryers, but they're expensive and take more time. So, I looked into a dishwasher with only basic features and ended up buying this one. We set a date, and the LG technician came, installed it, and explained everything to me. He told me to clean it with salt every two months, and to clean other parts once a month. It seemed like a lot more work than I expected, so I wondered if I'd made a bad purchase. But after I finished loading all my dinner dishes, I realized it was still convenient. (You can still put food in it, but it's better to soak it in water and leave it clean. I read somewhere that if you don't, food will collect at the bottom, making cleaning more difficult.) First, there's space for utensils, chopsticks, and tongs. The second and third compartments are also spacious, so pots can fit easily. There are separate compartments for solid and powder detergents. I included a photo of the solid detergent compartment in my review. On default mode, it runs for about 55 minutes and the door opens automatically, but it opens only slightly, so manually opening it seems to be the key to proper drying. Prices on Coupang change daily, so unless you're in a hurry, put it in your cart and buy it on the cheapest day with a strong credit card discount. A tip: I had a moving date, so I bought it in advance. Then, I saw a cheaper price in the middle of the process. I canceled the first item and repurchased the cheaper one. I was able to cancel with two days left, so I exclaimed, "Oh, Coupang!" Also, my sink is a bit high, so I had to reinforce the upper part for 30,000 won. I asked if they wanted to reinforce the lower part where the sink rises, but they said they wouldn't, because the lower part is hard to see and the door is always open. No one wants to look under my dishwasher, so I'd rather it be flat. This was a review of my aunt's dishwasher purchase with her own money!

There are more expensive dishwashers with hot air dryers, but they're expensive and take more time. So, I looked into a dishwasher with only basic features and ended up buying this one. We set a date, and the LG technician came, installed it, and explained everything to me. He told me to clean it with salt every two months, and to clean other parts once a month. It seemed like a lot more work than I expected, so I wondered if I'd made a bad purchase. But after I finished loading all my dinner dishes, I realized it was still convenient. (You can still put food in it, but it's better to soak it in water and leave it clean. I read somewhere that if you don't, food will collect at the bottom, making cleaning more difficult.) First, there's space for utensils, chopsticks, and tongs. The second and third compartments are also spacious, so pots can fit easily. There are separate compartments for solid and powder detergents. I included a photo of the solid detergent compartment in my review. On default mode, it runs for about 55 minutes and the door opens automatically, but it opens only slightly, so manually opening it seems to be the key to proper drying. Prices on Coupang change daily, so unless you're in a hurry, put it in your cart and buy it on the cheapest day with a strong credit card discount. A tip: I had a moving date, so I bought it in advance. Then, I saw a cheaper price in the middle of the process. I canceled the first item and repurchased the cheaper one. I was able to cancel with two days left, so I exclaimed, "Oh, Coupang!" Also, my sink is a bit high, so I had to reinforce the upper part for 30,000 won. I asked if they wanted to reinforce the lower part where the sink rises, but they said they wouldn't, because the lower part is hard to see and the door is always open. No one wants to look under my dishwasher, so I'd rather it be flat. This was a review of my aunt's dishwasher purchase with her own money!

There are more expensive dishwashers with hot air dryers, but they're expensive and take more time. So, I looked into a dishwasher with only basic features and ended up buying this one. We set a date, and the LG technician came, installed it, and explained everything to me. He told me to clean it with salt every two months, and to clean other parts once a month. It seemed like a lot more work than I expected, so I wondered if I'd made a bad purchase. But after I finished loading all my dinner dishes, I realized it was still convenient. (You can still put food in it, but it's better to soak it in water and leave it clean. I read somewhere that if you don't, food will collect at the bottom, making cleaning more difficult.) First, there's space for utensils, chopsticks, and tongs. The second and third compartments are also spacious, so pots can fit easily. There are separate compartments for solid and powder detergents. I included a photo of the solid detergent compartment in my review. On default mode, it runs for about 55 minutes and the door opens automatically, but it opens only slightly, so manually opening it seems to be the key to proper drying. Prices on Coupang change daily, so unless you're in a hurry, put it in your cart and buy it on the cheapest day with a strong credit card discount. A tip: I had a moving date, so I bought it in advance. Then, I saw a cheaper price in the middle of the process. I canceled the first item and repurchased the cheaper one. I was able to cancel with two days left, so I exclaimed, "Oh, Coupang!" Also, my sink is a bit high, so I had to reinforce the upper part for 30,000 won. I asked if they wanted to reinforce the lower part where the sink rises, but they said they wouldn't, because the lower part is hard to see and the door is always open. No one wants to look under my dishwasher, so I'd rather it be flat. This was a review of my aunt's dishwasher purchase with her own money!

There are more expensive dishwashers with hot air dryers, but they're expensive and take more time. So, I looked into a dishwasher with only basic features and ended up buying this one. We set a date, and the LG technician came, installed it, and explained everything to me. He told me to clean it with salt every two months, and to clean other parts once a month. It seemed like a lot more work than I expected, so I wondered if I'd made a bad purchase. But after I finished loading all my dinner dishes, I realized it was still convenient. (You can still put food in it, but it's better to soak it in water and leave it clean. I read somewhere that if you don't, food will collect at the bottom, making cleaning more difficult.) First, there's space for utensils, chopsticks, and tongs. The second and third compartments are also spacious, so pots can fit easily. There are separate compartments for solid and powder detergents. I included a photo of the solid detergent compartment in my review. On default mode, it runs for about 55 minutes and the door opens automatically, but it opens only slightly, so manually opening it seems to be the key to proper drying. Prices on Coupang change daily, so unless you're in a hurry, put it in your cart and buy it on the cheapest day with a strong credit card discount. A tip: I had a moving date, so I bought it in advance. Then, I saw a cheaper price in the middle of the process. I canceled the first item and repurchased the cheaper one. I was able to cancel with two days left, so I exclaimed, "Oh, Coupang!" Also, my sink is a bit high, so I had to reinforce the upper part for 30,000 won. I asked if they wanted to reinforce the lower part where the sink rises, but they said they wouldn't, because the lower part is hard to see and the door is always open. No one wants to look under my dishwasher, so I'd rather it be flat. This was a review of my aunt's dishwasher purchase with her own money!
